5.6.21: Hath yielded up his body to the grave;
5.6.22: But here is Carlisle living, to abide
5.6.23: Thy kingly doom and sentence of his pride.
5.6.25: Choose out some secret place, some reverend room,
5.6.26: More than thou hast, and with it joy thy life;
5.6.27: So as thou livest in peace, die free from strife:
5.6.28: For though mine enemy thou hast ever been,
5.6.29: High sparks of honour in thee have I seen.
5.6.30: Great king, within this coffin I present
5.6.31: Thy buried fear: herein all breathless lies
5.6.32: The mightiest of thy greatest enemies,
5.6.33: Richard of Bordeaux, by me hither brought.
5.6.34: Exton, I thank thee not; for thou hast wrought
5.6.35: A deed of slander with thy fatal hand
5.6.36: Upon my head and all this famous land.
5.6.37: From your own mouth, my lord, did I this deed.
5.6.38: They love not poison that do poison need,
5.6.39: Nor do I thee: though I did wish him dead,
5.6.40: I hate the murderer, love him murdered.
5.6.41: The guilt of conscience take thou for thy labour,
5.6.42: But neither my good word nor princely favour:
5.6.43: With Cain go wander through shades of night,
5.6.44: And never show thy head by day nor light.
5.6.45: Lords, I protest, my soul is full of woe,
5.6.46: That blood should sprinkle me to make me grow:
5.6.47: Come, mourn with me for that I do lament,
5.6.48: And put on sullen black incontinent:
5.6.49: I’ll make a voyage to the Holy Land,
5.6.50: To wash this blood off from my guilty hand:
5.6.51: March sadly after; grace my mournings here;
5.6.52: In weeping after this untimely bier.
